results.raw_content: Explore Other Pathways to New York State Financial Aid New York State offers multiple pathways to access state-funded financial aid without completing the FAFSA. Both the NYS DREAM Act and the Alternate Eligibility Pathway provide similar financial aid opportunities, though each has unique eligibility criteria. Here’s what you need to know about both options: The NYS DREAM Act Pathway The DREAM Act gives students who received their high school degree or GED in New York State and students receiving in-state tuition, including undocumented students, access to New York State administered student financial aid to support their higher education costs. What is the DREAM Act? The Senator José Peralta DREAM Act is not a financial aid application itself—it’s a pathway that allows certain students to apply for New York State financial aid. Once approved through the DREAM Act, you may be eligible to apply for programs such as: • Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) • Excelsior Scholarship • Enhanced Tuition Award • STEM Incentive Program • And more Who is Eligible? You may be eligible if you meet the following citizenship and educational criteria: Accepted Citizenship Statuses: • T Visa holder • U Visa holder • Temporary Protected Status (TPS) • DACA recipient • Pending lawful immigration status • US Citizens and Permanent residents whose permanent home is outside of NYS Educational Requirements: • Graduated from a New York State high school after attending for at least two years • Received a NYS high school equivalency diploma • Were charged in-state tuition at a SUNY or CUNY campus for reasons other than residency Where to Apply: Apply at: hesc.ny.gov/DREAM When to Apply: This application is open year-round since it is not a traditional financial aid application Need help? Join one of our upcoming Support Sessions to get your questions answered. These live, virtual sessions— hosted by HESC experts—will walk you through the application process, clarify eligibility criteria, and provide personalized guidance. Find and register for a session here: www.hesc.ny.gov/get-help/find-event 99 Washington Avenue, Albany, NY 12255 | hesc.ny.gov The Alternate Eligibility Pathway What Is the Alternate Pathway? New York State understands that some students— particularly those with family members who have different immigration statuses—may have concerns about sharing personal information through the FAFSA. To ensure equity and privacy, we’ve created an alternate pathway that allows eligible students to apply for state financial aid without submitting a FAFSA. This option offers a secure and accessible process that protects personal data while connecting students with the support they need. Who is Eligible? You may qualify for the Alternate Pathway if: • You are a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen • You are a NYS resident AND • You have at least one parent or spouse who is not a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen Where to Apply: Apply at: hesc.ny.gov/altpath When to Apply: This application is available year-round Need help? Attend one of our Support Sessions for personalized help. Our knowledgeable staff will guide you through the application process, answer your questions, and ensure you understand your financial aid options. Find and register for a session here: www.hesc.ny.gov/get-help/find-event Important Note: Students approved for aid through the Alternate Pathway are not eligible for the Excelsior Scholarship or the Enhanced Tuition Award. However, you’re free to change your mind. If you begin receiving TAP through the Alternate Pathway and later decide to apply for federal aid, you can complete the FAFSA at any time. You won’t need to reapply for TAP. 99 Washington Avenue, Albany, NY 12255 | hesc.ny.gov

# José Peralta New York State Dream Act

* [Office of Student Financial Assistance](https://www.cuny.edu/financial-aid/)
* [Applying for Financial Aid](https://www.cuny.edu/financial-aid/applying-for-financial-aid/)
* José Peralta New York State Dream Act



TAP – State Financial Aid for Undocumented Students  
 **Move Forward With Your Dreams!**

The José Peralta New York State DREAM Act allows undocumented and other students access to New York State‐administered grants and scholarships that support their higher education costs. If you attended or graduated from an NYS high school, attended an approved NYS high school equivalency program, or received an NYS equivalency diploma, you **may** be eligible for state financial aid.

The DREAM Act opens the doors of higher education and provides access to the *Excelsior Scholarship, the Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) and other state‐administered scholarships including Opportunity Programs.*

**Currently enrolled CUNY students:** You have until the end of the academic year to apply for state aid. This means you can still get funds for the Fall semester of the same academic year, even if you already paid for it!

**Not enrolled yet?** No problem! You can start your application now and finish when you receive your high school diploma. Or opt to have NYC Public School validate your diploma for you, but be sure to check back before the school year starts. Get started today!

[Review your eligibility and Apply](http://www.hesc.ny.gov/dream/)

## Steps to Apply

**Successfully Apply to TAP and other State Funded Programs**

#### [1. Determine Your Eligibilty](#1675885411601-59dbdbf6-01df)

There are **two** ways you can be eligible for the New York State DREAM Act, if your permanent home is in NYS and if you permanent home is NOT in NY.

LEAD Coalition created a eligibility flow chart and video guide. Take a look at it to determine your eligibility:

* [NYS Dream Act Module 2 – Eligibility and State Funding](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5c3676da3e2d09759ab10f10/t/5dde09d0c9bded2bd44c2bf7/1574832620919/Module+2.pdf)
* [Eligibility Flow Chart](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5c3676da3e2d09759ab10f10/t/5de58c65e59abc3a72e16e24/1575324774584/LEAD+Co+Eligibility+Flow+Chart--FINAL.pdf)

#### [2. Apply for the York State Dream Act and TAP](#1675885411676-11343fb7-c585)

To be eligible for TAP as an undocumented student you have to submit **TWO** applications, 1. the New York State Dream Act and 2. the Tuition Assistance Program application. *This second application will be submitted through the New York State Dream Act portal*. To see what this looks like take a look at the walk through below.

* [NYS Dream Act Preview Walkthrough by Adelante Student Voices](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/e/2PACX-1vS8T9fUMqfxSnhQ3bOf3JzNBRPc6UlAc6r8yMVtU2tvoi27zsmjRV1F-oFSDD3WMg/pub?start=true&loop=false&delayms=60000&slide=id.g5d345cd836_0_0)

The NYS Dream Act application also may require you to submit documents based on your immigration status. If you are unsure what documents to submit check out the document below.

* [NYS Dream Act Supporting Documents](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5c3676da3e2d09759ab10f10/t/5dda0df801a5762011752bc9/1574571513762/NYS+DREAM+Act+Supporting+Documents.pdf)

#### [3. Monitor your Application](#1675885448048-15a3dea4-3e40)

Congratulations! You submitted you application to receive state aid for college!

Be sure to visit your portal often to check if you need to provide additional information or confirm that your application has been reviewed.

If you need to update anything on the application please reach out to ISTS: [NYSDREAM@applyISTS.com](mailto:NYSDREAM@applyISTS.com)

If you have not heard back about your application please reach out to [dreamactcc@hesc.ny.gov](mailto:dreamactcc@hesc.ny.gov)

If you reached out to either of the two resources above and have not heard back or your campus has not received you TAP award please fill out the following survey and someone from [CUNY Immigrant Student Success](http://cuny.edu/immigrant) will reach out to you.

[Get help for completed applications](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdhQSuUijStq17pmZVUfHbZ5kXl6bihKRxXpVIPKuowNYwDOw/viewform)

![CUNY infographic showing support for immigrant and undocumented students with TAP and Dream Act](https://www.cuny.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/page-assets/financial-aid/applying-for-financial-aid/jose-peralta-new-york-state-dream-act/Queries-about-the-New-York-State-Dream-Act.png "Queries about the New York State Dream Act")

#### [4. Consider applying to other State funded Programs](#1675885483950-c5f95a72-0009)

In addition to TAP, the New York State Dream Act also makes you eligible for Opportunity Programs like ASAP, CD, or SEEK. This is a new legislation so some of our campuses may not be up to date on this information. Please visit our guide to help you access state funds provide by ASAP, CD, and SEEK.

* [Immigrant Students + ASAP CD SEEK](https://www.cuny.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/page-assets/current-students/student-affairs/cuny-immigrant-student-success/Immigrant-Students-CD-_-SEEK.pdf)

## Resources

Worksheet:

[Tips to Navigate the NYSDA](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_1itpeDq5rVoWKf18wdwOWNGm2R6fIux/view)

Contact Us:

[Get Help Accessing NYSDA Funds](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdhQSuUijStq17pmZVUfHbZ5kXl6bihKRxXpVIPKuowNYwDOw/viewform)

Info Sheet

[Undocumented Students & Excelsior Scholarship](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Wva6KoYb2EKHaMc8IBRNYDtDpd5e74Xk/view)

## What is State Aid?

**Are you not sure what State Aid means?**

The New York State Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) helps eligible New York residents pay tuition at approved schools in New York State. An annual TAP award can be as much as $5,665! Because TAP is a grant, it doesn’t have to be paid back.

Check out the video below for more information. Be sure to check out additional resources below to learn how to apply for state aid as an undocumented student.

![CUNY student activists](https://www.cuny.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/page-assets/financial-aid/applying-for-financial-aid/jose-peralta-new-york-state-dream-act/NYSDREAM-ACT.png "CUNY Dreamers, Dream Act Now")

CUNY student activists who organized, protested and advocated for the passage of this legislation for more than 10 years

![Chancellor Félix V. Matos Rodríguez](https://www.cuny.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/page-assets/about/chancellor/Chancellor-FelixVMatosRodriguez-Fall2022-SQ.jpeg "Chancellor Félix V. Matos Rodríguez")

“CUNY stands ready to have as many dreamers as possible take advantage of this historic opportunity.”  
 – Chancellor Félix V. Matos Rodríguez
